title: fix(create-plugin): take the defaults on cancel and on a non-TTY run (objectui#8786)
body:
Fixes #8786

Cancelling at `Plugin description:` or `Author name:` crashed the generator with a `TypeError` and left an empty `packages/plugin-NAME/` behind; and the published README's promise that a non-interactive run "takes MIT and still writes the text" was false — such a run wrote nothing at all and exited 0 in silence. Both are now one rule.

## The two premises this card's direction hangs on — measured first

The dispatching seat ruled direction **(i)** (make the non-TTY claim true) conditional on two premises, either of which being false meant stopping. Both hold:

- **P1 — the README really ships.** `packages/create-plugin/package.json` lists `"files": ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "LICENSE"]`, so `README.md` is in the tarball by explicit declaration (and by npm's default inclusion regardless). The false sentence is a **published** one. ✅
- **P2 — ruling C's fourth clause is a ruling, not a description.** objectui#8041 comment 5583986682 carries it in the ruling's own headline — "the scaffolder asks for the licence, defaults to MIT, and writes the matching LICENSE text; **non-interactive runs take the default**" — and again inside the `**Ruled.**` paragraph: "`--yes` / non-TTY runs take MIT and write the text". ✅

## What was measured on `origin/main` (4e3a4f07e), driven through a real pty and a pipe

| run | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cancel at `Plugin description:` | `TypeError`, exit 1, empty dir left | 10 files, MIT, exit 0 |
| cancel at `Author name:` | `TypeError`, exit 1, empty dir left | 10 files, MIT, exit 0 |
| cancel at `License:` **(control)** | 10 files, MIT, exit 0 | **10 files, MIT, exit 0 — unchanged** |
| all four answered | 10 files, exit 0 | unchanged |
| stdin from `/dev/null` | **nothing written**, exit 0, silent | 10 files, MIT, exit 0 |
| stdin from `/dev/null`, no name | nothing written, exit 0, **silent** | nothing written, exit 1, `Plugin name is required` |

## The repair

- **`prompts` returns a short answers object.** A cancelled question and every question after it are simply absent, so `answers.author` was `undefined` and `licenseCopyrightHolder` dereferenced `.trim()` on it. Both text answers are now merged against the same `initial` their prompt offered — one default written down once — and `PluginAnswers` types them optional, so reading one raw no longer compiles.
- **A non-TTY stdin is detected before `prompts` is called, not after.** `prompts` never settles there: readline reports EOF, neither `submit` nor `abort` ever fires, and the process runs out of work. There is no result to inspect, which is why the check has to come first.
- **Templating moved ahead of `fs.mkdirpSync`.** Nothing is created on disk until every file's contents exists, so no throw inside `buildPluginFiles` can leave a half-created directory for the retry to trip over. That makes the "empty directory" half of the card unreachable by construction rather than merely unreached.
- **The plugin name keeps its own behaviour** as the one answer with no default — but now says so. Previously a non-TTY run without a name exited 0 having printed nothing.

`README.md` gains a section stating the single rule, and `content/docs/utilities/create-plugin.mdx` gains the paragraph its Rule #2 counterpart owes.

## Tests — the gate this regression walked through

`src/index.ts` calls `program.parse()` at import time, so every existing test in this package stops at `buildPluginFiles` — and a `buildPluginFiles` test is green on **both** sides of this defect. The new `src/__tests__/cli-cancel-and-nontty-8786.test.ts` therefore drives the built bin: `script(1)` for a real pty where a cancel exists to be made, an ordinary closed pipe for the non-TTY runs. It rebuilds `dist/` unconditionally in `beforeAll` (scrubbing `VITEST`, per objectui#8598) so it can never assert about a stale bundle.

At `4ae7e7c6f`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/create-plugin/` — **Test Files 3 passed (3) · Tests 36 passed (36)**, the new file contributing 7. `templates.test.ts`'s ten-key set and `licenses.test.ts` are among them and stay green.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/create-plugin type-check` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, both legs echoed).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/create-plugin lint` — exit 0; `eslint --format json` reports **7 files judged, 0 errors, 0 warnings** — the whole of this package's TypeScript, the new test file included. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI: this narrowing excludes nothing, because `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so no untouched file's verdict can move on this diff.
- Gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-doc-links`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `tsconfig-test-parity-census` — all exit 0. Ratchets that judge the new test file — `spawned-build-vitest-env-8598`, `vitest-invocation-guard`, `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273` — 50 tests passed.

### Ablation — the new tests are shown to be able to fail, from the committed tree

Each leg mutated `src/index.ts`, proved the change landed on disk (anchor counts plus the blob hash), rebuilt, proved it reached `dist/index.js`, ran, then restored with `git checkout HEAD --` and proved the restore by `git diff HEAD` being empty **and** the blob matching, with a rebuild proving the mutated form was gone from `dist/` too.

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| **A1a** | drop the merge: `author: answers.author` | **NOT MEASURED** — the build refuses it, `TS2322: Type 'string \| undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'`. A reading in its own right: the repair is compiler-enforced, so the exact regression cannot come back silently. |
| **A1b** | same, cast so it compiles | **4 failed / 3 passed** — both early cancels and both writing non-TTY runs red with `TypeError`. Green: the `License:` cancel **(control)**, the answered run, and the name-required run (it exits before the merge). |
| **A2** | ablate the non-TTY detection so every run is treated as interactive | **3 failed / 4 passed** — only the three non-TTY cases red. Every pty leg, control included, stays green. |

Clean rerun after each restore: **7 passed**. ⭐ The `License:` cancel is green in **both** legs, which is what makes it a control rather than a companion that reds whenever anything breaks.

## Position axis (objectui#8875)

**Zero class-(A) citations** — no in-tree `file:line` reference is moved by this diff. `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs --json` finds exactly two citations resolving into this package, and both address `templates.ts` / `templates.test.ts`, neither of which this diff touches; the census's own totals are unchanged. The line addresses in card #8786's own body (an issue body, not a tree file) do go stale as this lands, by construction. Everything else belongs to objectui#8875 / PR #8881 and is deliberately untouched here, `CHANGELOG.md` line references included.

## Changeset

`@object-ui/create-plugin` `minor` — the non-TTY default path is published behaviour that grows. ⛔ Never `major` (39 packages in one `fixed` group). The pending `.changeset/8041-create-plugin-licence-prompt.md` needs no correction: its sentence "A non-interactive run takes MIT and still writes the text" is true as of this PR rather than before it.

## 验收备注

**Out of scope, filed separately: objectui#8892.** `buildLicenseFile`'s docblock argues its MIT fallback makes "a manifest claiming a licence with no text beside it" unreachable "by any route, including a future caller that builds `PluginTemplateVars` by hand", and closes "the manifest is written from the same resolved id, so the two still agree". That last sentence is false: `buildPackageJson` writes `vars.license` verbatim and nothing resolves it a second time, so a hand-built `{ license: 'NOT-A-LICENCE' }` yields a manifest naming it beside MIT text. Internal-only today — the package is `bin`-only and the CLI is the sole caller, passing `resolveLicenseId`'s total output. This PR does not touch either function, so it does not falsify that docblock; it is not carried here, per the dispatching seat's ruling. objectui#8892 records it with three directions and no verdict.

**Not reopened:** the licence set (four licences, no free text) is the maintainer's call, and objectui#8778 (copyright holder in the four emitted source headers) stays separate — neither is addressed here.

**Noted, not filed.** `content/docs/utilities/create-plugin.mdx` still enumerates the prompts as "a description and an author" — the licence question objectui#8041 added as the fourth prompt is absent from that sentence, which predates this card and is objectui#8779's documentation debt, not this one's. It sits directly above the paragraph this PR adds, so it is worth a line rather than silence; ⛔ not repaired here, because establishing that no other claim holds that file costs more than the sentence is worth and the dispatch's scope red line is explicit. Successor: the next PR touching `content/docs/utilities/create-plugin.mdx`, or a docs pass over objectui#8041's landing.

Seat session for this implementation: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01611D6ZaRaMmwTNQmSbk8MH`.

**Clause-② is `yes`**, judged on the delivered diff: the emitted file set and the prompt behaviour of the scaffolder are its published behaviour, in ruling C's own words, and this diff changes what both do on two of the runs a user can perform. No new exported symbol (the package is `bin`-only, with no `exports`), and no new key on a published payload — the `yes` rests on the behaviour limb. `needs:contract-review` is on both carriers and this stays in draft until a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` verdict is on record.
